summary: The paper lets a Fortran 90D/HPF user name a partitioner that works from connectivity, coordinates or loads, so the compiler can distribute irregular arrays at run time. It also gives a conservative test that reuses inspector results when indirection arrays are unchanged.
why_read: It is an early, clear account of how a compiler can support irregular data distributions by calling partitioners and reusing run-time communication schedules.
main_contribution: Compiler directives that build a GeoCoL graph for user-chosen partitioners, plus a conservative run-time test for reusing inspector results in Fortran 90D/HPF loops.
main_limitation: The reuse test is conservative and can add high run-time overhead in some cases, and the results come from a single machine.
evaluation_method: measured execution time on Intel iPSC/860 against hand-coded versions
states_relationship_to: Das, Saltz and von Hanxleden slicing analysis
Ponnusamy et al. 1992 runtime mapping scheme
Ponnusamy et al. 1995 HPF irregular distributions
